issue.title: Cheaper monitor hops: starter reply and tool-call digest in the successor prompt, slot-reservation lease, no wait on post-kill bookkeeping
issue.description:
Proposed by phase sase-177.4 (epic sase-177; plan "Follow-ups" item 2). With Muse now
limited to 10-minute synchronous commands, more work goes through monitor hops, so each
hop should be cheaper:

- The monitor successor's prompt gets the starter agent's last reply plus a tool-call
  digest, so the successor does not re-derive context.
- A bounded, visible slot-reservation lease covers the hop so another agent cannot take
  the family's slot between starter exit and successor start.
- Successor dispatch stops waiting on the starter runner's post-kill bookkeeping
  (median ~77 s measured on athena Sep 20-23).
